ARABIC — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Avoid speaking to classmates
   B. Mix random languages with no purpose
   C. Only memorise without using the language
   D. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

2. When practising Conversational Skills: Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Conversational Skills: Etiquette.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational Skills: Etiquette.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational Skills: Etiquette.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Conversational Skills: Etiquette.

3. When practising Public Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Public Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Public Speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Public Speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Public Speaking.

4. When practising Conversational Skills: Interviews, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Conversational Skills: Interviews.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational Skills: Interviews.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Conversational Skills: Interviews.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational Skills: Interviews.

5. When practising Intensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Listening.

6. When practising Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading Fluency.

7. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.

8. When practising Comprehension and Critical Reading Skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension and Critical Reading Skills.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension and Critical Reading Skills.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension and Critical Reading Skills.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension and Critical Reading Skills.

9. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.

10. When practising Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription.

11. When practising Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
12. In three clear sentences, explain Comprehension and Critical Reading Skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Study Skills: The Reading Process and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Mechanics of Writing: The Arabic Calligraphy and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Social Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Functional Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Creative Writing: Poems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Narrative and Dramatic Writing Skills: Stories and Skits and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Professional and Business Writing Skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Vocabulary Building and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
